source.title: MINT: A Universal Zero-Shot Predictor for Transaction Data
source.authors: Parameswaran Kamalaruban; Viktor Drobnyi; Maeve Madigan; Julia Rozanova; David Sutton; Stuart Burrell

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether modality projection preserves task-relevant information in transaction representations, using linear-classifier accuracy rather than a direct representation-similarity measure.
record.gate_note: The section 6.4 projection analysis directly measures task accuracy from original and projected transaction embeddings, so those results bear narrowly on V4. The QA benchmark, model-scaling, and efficiency results do not measure representation convergence or interchangeability and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses a trained MLP connector to project transaction-encoder embeddings into an LLM input space, as a component of its own QA system. It reports only its method's performance. The section 6.4 probe checks whether task information survives a learned projection. It does not measure whether two independently trained models' representations align or map onto each other with little loss. A trained MLP keeping linearly decodable task signal is not evidence of interchangeable representations. No convergence, alignment or similarity between the transaction encoder and the LLM is measured, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase fits only the section 6.4 projection analysis: the authors say both projectors preserve most task-relevant signal with modest degradation. The paper's main conclusion is different. Injecting compact transaction embeddings into an LLM beats text serialization on predictive QA, in distribution and out of distribution, with lower token, latency and memory costs. Text serialization stays stronger for in-distribution extractive QA. The authors draw no conclusion about representation convergence.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses an MLP connector for transaction-to-LLM modality projection and evaluates downstream linear-classifier accuracy; it does not apply a representation-convergence measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported probe accuracy depends on projection method (MINT projector versus contrastive alignment model) and task (extractive versus predictive QA).

fits_no_version.finding: Linear probes on embeddings after a learned projection keep most task accuracy relative to the original embeddings. The MINT MLP projector gives 0.724/0.74 vs 0.756/0.752; the contrastive projection gives 0.766/0.732.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned modality connectors that map a frozen domain encoder into an LLM input space preserve most linearly decodable task information.

record.problems: The representation comparison is indirect: it measures downstream linear-classifier accuracy rather than representational similarity or interchangeability. No uncertainty estimates are reported for these probe results.
record.rows_left_out: Main QA benchmark, scaling, and efficiency results are not included because they do not measure representation convergence or mapped-representation preservation. Section 6.4 reports additional ablations and benchmark evaluations that likewise do not directly test the versions catalogued here.
record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 and its V4 'supports' labels are dropped. The MINT connector is an MLP trained end-to-end for compatibility with a frozen LLM, and the probe only asks whether information survives that learned map. No similarity metric, cross-model comparison, scaling of alignment, or seed comparison appears. Table 3 varies LLM and encoder size, but only for QA accuracy, not alignment, so it does not bear on V1. No uncertainty is reported, and the data are proprietary.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of representational alignment across model sizes or capability levels.
No measurement of alignment between image and caption representations as models improve.
No comparison of representations across random seeds or shared features/subspaces.

Tests preservation of task-relevant information after projection, not direct representational similarity or interchangeability between transaction-encoder and LLM representations. The MINT projector is an MLP, not a linear map.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are identified across models.
No comparison of representation similarity measures, their settings, or input distributions.
No test of whether convergence is incomplete, plateaus, or is explained by shared training data or objectives.

rows.note: The study describes the degradation relative to original embeddings as modest.

rows.subject: MINT projector
rows.operation_detail: Linear classifiers were trained on transaction embeddings after MINT projection.
rows.note: The study describes the degradation relative to original embeddings as modest.
rows.check: This is a task-signal retention probe of the study's own connector (0.74 vs 0.752). It does not measure cross-model interchangeability.

rows.subject: contrastive alignment model
rows.operation_detail: Linear classifiers were trained on transaction embeddings after contrastive alignment projection.
rows.note: The projected-embedding probe accuracy is close to the original-embedding reference.
rows.check: The contrastive alignment baseline's projection head is trained jointly with a text projection head. A probe on its output (0.766) does not measure how well the transaction and text spaces map onto each other.
